title: Environment configuration
description: Schema for environments/<name>/config.yaml — flat capability sections. Secrets never live here; they belong in the sibling .env file.

dtk_version.description: DTK release this environment is written against. Asserted against the clone's actual git tag at apply time; a mismatch fails, it does not warn. This is what keeps 'matched versions only' true now that env repos and the DTK clone version independently.

name.description: Cluster identity — defaults to the environment directory name. Durable: it becomes the external-dns TXT owner id, backup prefixes, and VM name prefix. Do not change it on an existing cluster.

role.description: Determines which gitops paths are deployed and which template directory is used

lb_ipam.description: Cilium LB IPAM — one dedicated single-IP pool per gateway (on-prem). Required for on-prem providers.

pools.description: Per-gateway address pools. gw-int and gw-ext apply to every role; gw-extapi and gw-intapi are required on role 'hub' and rejected elsewhere. These pools are the cluster's entire load-balancer address supply.

lan.description: Address the pool hands to this gateway's LoadBalancer Service, announced via L2 on the LAN

wan.description: Optional outside address the border firewall 1:1-DNATs to lan. Becomes the external-dns target for everything attached to the gateway; LAN clients then need hairpin NAT or split DNS.

infra.description: Infrastructure provider settings Talos node OS facts (nameservers, NTP) live in <env>/talos.yaml.

proxmox.description: Proxmox provider selection. Placement lives in <env>/placement.yaml; network_bridge and storage pools in <env>/proxmox/proxmox.yaml.

aws.description: AWS provider settings. Credentials come from .env (AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID / AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY / AWS_REGION); this block carries only structural facts.

region.description: AWS region the cluster deploys into (e.g. eu-west-1). Stated, never defaulted: a wrong implicit region builds the cluster somewhere the operator is not looking.

api_allowed_cidrs.description: CIDRs allowed to reach the public EKS API endpoint. Required and non-empty by decision (emptiness enforced by the aws module's variable validation — the in-house validator has no minItems): the API server never sits open to 0.0.0.0/0. An operator with a changing address lists their current CIDR and re-applies when it moves.

dns.description: DNS zone management. Credentials in .env (DIGITALOCEAN_TOKEN, CLOUDFLARE_API_TOKEN, or AWS_* for route53).

cert.description: Certificates (ACME). The CA is selected by server alone; where it requires External Account Binding, set ACME_EAB_KEY_ID and ACME_EAB_HMAC_ENCODED in .env.

email.description: ACME account contact — where the CA sends expiry and revocation notices. Required rather than defaulted: the old admin@<dns.domain> fallback named a mailbox the toolkit invented and nobody necessarily reads, so expiry warnings could arrive nowhere.

server.description: ACME directory URL — this alone selects the CA; there is no provider name to choose. Required rather than defaulted, so the authority every platform certificate is issued from is visible in the config. Examples: https://acme-v02.api.letsencrypt.org/directory, https://dv.acme-v02.api.pki.goog/directory (Google Trust Services), https://acme.zerossl.com/v2/DV90 (ZeroSSL). Any CA other than Let's Encrypt also needs EAB credentials in .env.

artifact.description: Distribution gitops artifact consumed by Flux. Credentials OCI_REPO_* in .env. url and version are both required — the version is a pin, never defaulted.

version.description: OCI tag — must be a pinned version (vX.Y.Z). 'latest' is disallowed: it contradicts matched-versions-only and the version assert cannot check a moving target.

active.description: Enable Flux OCI reconciliation (default: true when url is set)

verify.description: Cosign signature verification on the OCIRepository (spec.verify, provider cosign). Default false — the distribution's signing infrastructure does not exist yet; flip it on once artifacts are signed. Keyless verification unless verify_secret names a Secret of cosign public keys.

verify_secret.description: Name of a Secret (flux-system namespace, adopter-created) holding cosign public keys for verification; only meaningful with verify: true. Absent = keyless verification.

registry.description: Container image pull-through cache. Credentials OCI_PROXY_* in .env.

enabled.description: Whether this cluster pulls images through a registry mirror. When true, url is required (enforced as a Terraform precondition, not by this schema). Independent of robots, which is tooling-role provisioning and applies regardless.

url.description: Registry URL, stated outright — no oci:// prefix (this becomes a Talos registry mirror endpoint). Required when enabled is true.

robots.description: tooling role only: pull-only robot accounts to provision in the toolkit Harbor, one per consuming Hub (convention: name = the Hub's cluster.name). The Hub authenticates as robot-<name>; 'make secrets' prints the secret. Additive and creation-only — removing an entry never deletes the robot.

name.description: Robot account name (lowercase alphanumeric, '.', '_' or '-' separators)

enabled.description: Whether backups run at all. false disables them structurally (PSMDB/PXC backup+PITR off, vault-backup suspended) — PSMDB >=1.22 refuses to mark the cluster ready while PBM storage is unconfigured, so this must be a real switch and not an empty endpoint. Turning it on later restarts the mongod pods (PBM sidecars are added). When true, endpoint/bucket/region are required (enforced as a Terraform precondition, not by this schema). Independent of buckets, which is tooling-role provisioning.

endpoint.description: S3 endpoint URL, stated outright. Any S3-compatible service that speaks SigV4 with a static keypair and presents a publicly-trusted certificate — e.g. https://s3.eu-west-2.amazonaws.com, or a MinIO endpoint. Required when enabled is true.

bucket.description: Bucket name. Required when enabled is true — previously defaulted to 'backups', which silently sent this cluster's backups to a bucket nobody named.

region.description: S3 region, part of the SigV4 signature. Required when enabled is true — previously defaulted to 'us-east-1', which is wrong for most endpoints and fails at backup time rather than at plan time.

buckets.description: tooling role only: extra buckets to serve from the toolkit MinIO, each with a generated scoped user (access key = bucket name; 'make secrets' prints the secret key). System buckets (harbor, backups, thanos, loki, tempo) always exist and cannot be re-declared. Additive and creation-only — removing an entry never deletes data.

name.description: S3 bucket name (3-63 chars, lowercase alphanumeric, '.' or '-')

observability.description: Telemetry push sink. Alloy authenticates its push with basic auth from OBS_INGEST_USERNAME/PASSWORD in .env and verifies TLS — the URLs must present a publicly-trusted certificate (the Tooling Cluster's .ext ingest hostnames do).

enabled.description: Whether this cluster pushes logs, metrics and traces to an external sink. When true, all three URLs are required (enforced as a Terraform precondition, not by this schema).

ingest_users.description: tooling role only: telemetry-ingest accounts to provision in the obs-ingest front, one per pushing cluster (convention: name = the pushing cluster's cluster.name). The pusher authenticates as <name>; 'make secrets' prints the password. Independent of enabled — this cluster serves the sink rather than pushing to one. Additive and creation-only — removing an entry stops managing the account.

name.description: Ingest account name (lowercase alphanumeric, '.', '_' or '-' separators)

loki_url.description: Loki push URL, stated outright — e.g. https://loki.example.com/loki/api/v1/push. Required when enabled is true.

mimir_url.description: Prometheus remote-write URL, stated outright — e.g. https://thanos.example.com/api/v1/receive. Required when enabled is true.

tempo_url.description: OTLP trace push URL, stated outright — e.g. https://tempo.example.com/v1/traces. Required when enabled is true.

email.description: Transactional email (SMTP). Credentials SMTP_USER/SMTP_PASSWORD in .env. When the block exists, host, port and from are all required — the sender address is never invented (the old noreply@<domain> default silently broke SPF/DMARC) and the port is never assumed.

from.description: Sender address, stated outright — must be a mailbox/domain the SMTP account may send as.

starttls.description: Whether the relay negotiates STARTTLS. A plain in-cluster catcher states false; internet relays keep the default.

alerting.description: Alert delivery channels (Grafana contact points). Telegram token in .env. Each declared channel states its endpoint outright — the old alerts@example.invalid default routed alerts to a mailbox that cannot exist.

api_type.description: Mojaloop API dialect — set once at deploy time

hub.description: Hub identity and onboarding amounts — required in full on hub clusters (Terraform precondition; this schema requires the keys whenever the block exists). The old defaults (participant 'Hub', funds_in 100000, net_debit_cap 1000) were financial facts filled in silently.
